title: App shell
summary: The page frame: nav column, header, one scrolling body and footer. Header and footer stay put; safe-area insets are added on notched phones; a slotted control marked data-nav-toggle opens the side nav drawer, or hides and shows the nav on a wide screen.

props.name: navOpen
props.description: Drawer state, mirrors the side nav.

props.name: navHidden
props.description: Above the drawer breakpoint (1024px) the side nav is hidden and the body takes the full width; the nav toggle flips it and the nav comes back in its previous expanded or icon-rail state. Remembered under the nav's persist key plus ":nav-hidden". On a phone or tablet the nav is the drawer (navOpen) and this has no effect.

props.name: flush
props.description: Removes the body padding so a workspace, table or map sits edge to edge (the safe-area insets on a notched phone stay).

props.name: backHref
props.description: Puts a back link (an arrow) before the title: a same-site path or an http(s) address, usually the parent list. Empty shows no link. Anything else is dropped with a warning.

props.name: backLabel
props.description: The back link's accessible name (its aria-label), for example "Back to Invoices"; the arrow is the only visible content.

slots.name: title
slots.description: The page title in the top bar (a heading or plain text), after the back link and before the header slot; one line, truncated with an ellipsis. Put the page's only h1 here.

slots.name: header
slots.description: Top bar content after the title: page actions, an account menu. A direct child marked data-nav-toggle stays first.

events.name: pk-nav-toggle
events.description: A data-nav-toggle control was pressed (open is the drawer state, hidden the wide-screen state), or the saved nav visibility was restored.

writes.why: The nav-open state and the hamburger [data-nav-toggle] control the drawer state of the nav (and follow it). Not undone on disconnect. The wide-screen hide is done in the shell's own shadow tree (its nav slot), not on the nav.

a11y: Landmarks: header, main content region and footer are exposed; only the body scrolls, so there is never a nested scrollbar; the skip link belongs first in the header slot. The back link is a real link (keyboard reachable, 44px target, focus ring) named by back-label; the arrow is aria-hidden. Put the page's h1 in the title slot so there is exactly one page heading; do not repeat it in the body.
mobile: The nav becomes a drawer; the body padding narrows; env(safe-area-inset-*) keeps content clear of the notch and home bar. The back link keeps a 44px target and a long title is truncated to one line.
